subtitle: The Eye That Measured the Sky

panels.action: Vatasseri Parameśvara stands on a coastal Kerala hill near Alathiyur at dusk, palm-leaf manuscripts in one hand, the other raised toward a darkening sky where the moon nears the sun, the Nila valley stretching behind him.

dialogue.text: In fourteenth–fifteenth century Kerala, Vatasseri Parameśvara of Alathiyur watches the heavens for decades, reshaping computation through sight.

i18n.hi: चौदह–पंद्रहवीं सदी के केरल में अलथियूर के वात्तसेरी पारमेश्वरण दशकों तक आकाश देखते हैं, नज़र से हिसाब बदल देते हैं।

panels.action: A tranquil wide view of the Nila river valley in Kerala, coconut palms and tiled-roof houses, with a small shrine and a thatched study-hall where young Parameśvara sits cross-legged, eyes intent on a palm-leaf manuscript.

dialogue.text: On the banks of the Nila in Kerala, the Vatasseri family preserves learning, ritual, and the quiet craft of reckoning the heavens.

i18n.hi: केरल की नीला नदी किनारे वात्तसेरी कुल विद्या, अनुष्ठान और शांत आसमान-गणना की कला सँभालता है।

panels.action: Inside the study-hall, older Parameśvara sits before a low desk, palm leaves spread out, a stylus in hand; oil lamps flicker as he traces numbers beside verses describing planetary motions from Parahita tables.

dialogue.text: From earlier masters he inherits Parahita tables, numbers handed down, meant to serve all: tradition set in verse and digit.

i18n.hi: पुराने आचार्यों से उसे मिलती हैं परहित सारणियाँ—संख्याएँ जो सबकी सेवा को हैं, परंपरा जो श्लोक और अँकों में बँधी है।

panels.action: Close-up on Parameśvara’s weathered, contemplative face as he glances from the manuscript toward a small slit-window showing a bright moon, his brows slightly furrowed in doubt.

dialogue.text: Yet Parameśvara, pupil of Madhava, has learned to suspect numbers that do not meet the sky.

i18n.hi: पर माधव के शिष्य पारमेश्वरण ने वो संख्याएँ परखना सीख लिया है जो आसमान से मेल न खाएँ।

panels.action: In the open courtyard of the house at night, villagers and family stand together, faces turned upward; Parameśvara kneels near a simple gnomon and cord, marking shadows and positions as a partial lunar eclipse darkens the moon.

dialogue.text: During eclipses in the Nila valley, he does not merely watch in awe. He measures, notes, and remembers.

i18n.hi: नीला घाटी में ग्रहणों के समय वह सिर्फ चकित नहीं देखता—वह नापता है, लिखता है, याद रखता है।

panels.shot: medium shot over shoulder on manuscripts
panels.action: Over-the-shoulder view of Parameśvara sitting indoors the next day, comparing his fresh observation marks with columns of eclipse predictions in an older almanac, his hand hovering over a discrepancy.

dialogue.speaker: vatasseri_paramesvara
dialogue.text: The sky says one thing. The tables say another.

i18n.hi: आसमान कुछ कहता है, सारणियाँ कुछ और।

panels.action: His hands carefully inscribe neat lines on a new palm leaf labeled for eclipses, arranging dates, local times, and magnitudes in columns, leaving space for computed values beside them.

dialogue.text: So he begins a long record: eclipses seen in Alathiyur, each bound to numbers that claim to foretell them.

i18n.hi: तो वह लंबा ब्योरा शुरू करता है: अलथियूर में देखे हर ग्रहण को उन संख्याओं से बाँधता है जो उसे पहले से बताने का दावा करती हैं।

panels.action: A stylized wide panel showing Parameśvara in three ghosted poses across the same courtyard over years: younger, middle-aged, older, all observing different eclipses with simple instruments and assistants, the Nila valley subtly changing.

dialogue.text: Year after year, eclipse after eclipse, he watches. From about 1411 onward, Alathiyur becomes his observatory.

i18n.hi: साल पर साल, ग्रहण पर ग्रहण वह देखता रहता है। लगभग 1411 से अलथियूर ही उसका वेधशाला बन जाता है।

panels.action: In a dim room, Parameśvara sits with a small group of students; he points with his stylus at columns labeled "Observed" and "Computed" on a leaf, the students intent, some skeptical.

dialogue.text: He teaches that sight itself is a test. Parahita numbers, though revered, must bow if they fail it.

i18n.hi: वह सिखाता है कि खुद आँख ही कसौटी है। पूजनीय परहित संख्याएँ भी नाप में हारीं तो झुकेंगी।

panels.action: Close-up of a palm-leaf manuscript front leaf as Parameśvara inscribes its title; behind the script we see a small diagram of sun, moon, and earth etched: this is his Grahanamandana.

dialogue.text: From these efforts grows Grahanamandana, with an epoch set in 1411. Eclipses are no longer just portents, but tests.

i18n.hi: इन मेहनतों से 1411 की युग-तिथि वाला ‘ग्रहणमंडन’ उगता है। ग्रहण अब सिर्फ शकुन नहीं, परख बन जाते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot with scrolls and abacus-like counting
panels.action: Parameśvara sits surrounded by stacked palm-leaf bundles, counting on his fingers while sliding small seeds to keep track; he corrects constants and writes new verses, the strain of long work visible.

dialogue.text: Slowly, he adjusts the constants of the old Parahita system, letting observed eclipses pull the numbers into truer paths.

i18n.hi: धीर-धीरे वह पुराने परहित तंत्र के स्थिरांक सुधरता है, देखे गए ग्रहणों से संख्याओं को सही राह पर खींचता है।

panels.action: Low-angle view of Parameśvara rising from his mat, holding aloft a fresh manuscript bundle labeled internally with verses of Drigganita, his face lit by morning light entering through the doorway.

dialogue.text: By 1431, he completes Drigganita—"sight-computation"—a bold title that ties calculation to the act of seeing.

i18n.hi: 1431 तक वह ‘दृग्गणित’ पूरा कर लेता है—‘दृष्टि-गणना’—एक साहसी नाम जो हिसाब को देखने के काम से बाँध देता है।

panels.action: Parameśvara recites from Drigganita to young scholars, tracing a simple diagram of the earth’s shadow over the moon on the floor, linking verse to the earlier observations.

dialogue.speaker: vatasseri_paramesvara
dialogue.text: If computed eclipses match those seen, then our numbers are worthy. Otherwise, we change them.

i18n.hi: अगर निकाले गए ग्रहण देखे गए ग्रहण से मिलें तो हमारी संख्याएँ योग्य हैं। नहीं तो उन्हें बदलेंगे।

panels.action: Close on a palm leaf where Parameśvara has drawn a cyclic quadrilateral inside a circle, sides marked with small numerals, the circle’s radius highlighted by a bold etched line.

dialogue.text: He also turns to geometry, finding a rule for the circumradius of a cyclic quadrilateral—subtle, precise, and centuries ahead of distant Europe.

i18n.hi: वह ज्यामिति की ओर भी मुड़ता है, चक्रीय चतुर्भुज की परिधिवृत्त की त्रिज्या का नियम खोजता है—सूक्ष्म, सटीक, और दूर यूरोप से सदियाँ आगे।

panels.shot: wide shot with coastal horizon and star chart
panels.action: At night near the coast, Parameśvara stands by a low table holding a star chart; beyond him the Arabian Sea gleams, hinting at trade routes connecting Kerala to wider worlds.

dialogue.text: Kerala’s shores carry merchants and tales to distant lands. His mathematics, quiet on palm leaves, remains rooted here—for now.

i18n.hi: केरल के तट सौदागर और किस्से दूर देशों तक ले जाते हैं। उसका गणित, शांत ताड़पत्रों पर लिखा, अभी यहीं जड़ें जमाए रहता है।

panels.action: Older Parameśvara sits alone, shoulders slightly stooped, revisiting earlier observation leaves, occasionally correcting a verse in light of a newer eclipse record, a faint smile of satisfaction on his face.

dialogue.text: By the 1440s, with Goladipika completed, his corpus is large. What joins it is a single thread: the eye ruling the equation.

i18n.hi: 1440 के दशक तक ‘गोलदीपिका’ पूरी हो चुकी है, उसका ग्रंथ-संग्रह विशाल है। इन्हें जोड़ती है एक डोर: समीकरण पर राज करती आँख।

panels.action: A symbolic wide composition: a timeline suggested by rows of palm leaves from 1390s to 1440s, with Parameśvara’s figure at intervals, from youth to age, always turned toward eclipsed suns and moons rising over the Nila.

dialogue.text: Across roughly fifty-five years, he lets repeated eclipses grind against tradition, pushing Kerala computation toward a more exact form.

i18n.hi: करीब पचपन साल तक वह बार-बार के ग्रहणों को परंपरा से भिड़ने देता है, केरल की गणना को ज़्यादा सूक्ष्म रूप की ओर धकेलता है।

panels.action: A still life: neatly tied bundles of palm-leaf manuscripts labeled on their spines with small etched marks for Grahanamandana, Drigganita, Goladipika, resting beside a simple wooden observing rod, all bathed in soft afternoon light.

dialogue.text: Later scholars will copy and cite his texts. Through them, Parameśvara’s demand is clear: truth must listen to evidence, and even revered tables may change.

i18n.hi: आगे के पंडित उसके ग्रंथों को उतारेंगे, उद्धृत करेंगे। उनके ज़रिए पारमेश्वरण की माँग साफ है: सत्य को सबूत सुनना होगा, और पूजित सारणियाँ भी बदल सकती हैं।

title_i18n.hi: पारमेश्वरण की पचपन बरस की निगरानी

subtitle_i18n.en: The Eye That Measured the Sky
